selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer tracks supplements and workouts, and responds well to science-backed claims and ingredient transparency. This directly aligns with the advertiser's value of being science-backed and offering a healthy superfood snack.

The Gen Z Aesthete discovers through TikTok and Instagram, caring about packaging and brand voice, which provides a strong creative angle for a modern direct-to-consumer superfood snack targeting younger demographics.

The Fitness Enthusiast works out frequently and buys functional snacks and recovery products, making them a natural fit for a healthy makhana superfood snack that matches their performance-oriented lifestyle.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent loves subscriptions, whereas the advertiser's business model is explicitly a one-off purchase.
The Pet Parent focuses entirely on pet food and supplies, which has no overlap with human grocery snacks.
The Affluent Classic is disinterested in influencer positioning and trendy language, whereas a modern DTC superfood snack relies heavily on contemporary digital marketing.

The Sustainability Buyer focuses strictly on environmental footprints and supply chain transparency, whereas the advertiser's core differentiator is science-backed health rather than eco-certifications.
The Convenience-First Millennial relies on instant delivery and heavy subscription services, contradicting the advertiser's one-off purchase model.
The Value-Conscious Shopper requires discount-forward messaging and bundle offers, whereas the advertiser is positioned as a mid-tier superfood brand.
The Gifter is explicitly disinterested in self-care-only framing and relies on gifting holidays, whereas a daily grocery snack is an everyday self-purchase.
